lines: When articulating breath: first he rests
in heart-emptiness; then outside, from breath's
arising; then toward external, by apāna's
desiring no other; from samāna's arising,
l4.sanskrit_cite: tatra prāṇam uccicārayiṣuḥ pūrvaṃ hṛdaya eva śūnye viśrāmyati tato bāhye prāṇodayāt tato 'pi bāhyaṃ prati apānacandrāpūraṇena sarvātmatāṃ paśyati tataḥ anyanirākāṅkṣo bhavati tataḥ samānodayāt saṃghaṭṭaviśrāntim anubhavati tata udānavahnyudaye mātṛmeyādikalanāṃ grasate

reads_against.argmap: What is the prāṇa-uccāra sequence? → Six-stage articulation: hṛdaya-śūnya → prāṇodaya → apāna-candra → anya-nirākāṅkṣā → samāna-saṃghaṭṭa → udāna-kalanā.
c1_essence: Articulating breath: heart-emptiness → breath-arising outside → apāna-moon-filling all-selfness → desiring-no-other → samāna union-rest → udāna grasps measure-measured.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with abhyāsa weight (quiescence as disciplined practice)
